text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- A leading member of the People's Party, the conservative junior coalition partner, says the party only remains in the government because it has a responsibility to do so and not because it is loyal to the Social Democrats. The conservatives claim they were not informed about WestLB's first option on the City of Vienna's controlling stake in privatisation candidate Bank Austria.

- Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa says the political debate about the bank has damaged its image and threatens to take legal action against those "deliberately" inflicting damage on it. He claims the number of shares sold in a three billion capital increase was reduced by some 300 million schillings because of the debate.
- Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, state secretary of finance, says the government plans only minimal increases in civil servants' salaries.
- Chamber of Labour head Herbert Tumpel says employment targets have to be included in the Maastricht criteria before his organisation can support the introduction of Europe's single currency.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank head Christian Konrad says the debate about selling the entire City of Vienna stake in Bank Austria was "ridiculous" because such a sale would overstretch capital markets.
- Lower-than-expected tax revenues could cause a budget shortfall of between 14 and 18 billion schillings this year, the finance ministry says.
- Austria says the European Union must continue to pay subsidies to the country's less developed regions because of its geographical vicinity to eastern Europe.
- The government has yet to decide whether it will subsidise Austria's exporters with some 1.4 billion schillings.
- Swiss insurer Winterthur says it did not buy insurer EA-Generali's stake in Creditanstalt.
DIE PRESSE
- The finance ministry considers to increase tax rates on insurance in a bid to plug its budget holes.
- Raiffeisen chief Konrad says milk producers Bergland and Noem should merge quickly to realise synergies and help cut growing losses.

- Connect Austria, a bidder for Austria's third mobil phone licence, says it is considering taking legal action against the government because the deadline for bids was extended by one month to July 2nd even though it submitted an offer before the original deadline expired.
KURIER
- Auditors say they are considering to take legal action against the reformed minimum corporate tax rate, claiming it is still too high.
- Federal railway company OeBB's supervisory board has approved a 75 billion schillings order or 400 new locomotives until the year 2001. The company plans to cut up to 8,000 jobs.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Post & Telekom Austria will halve its charges for telephone calls to the U.S. to 6.60 schillings per minute from November 1.
